1._section_summary: This abstract describes a psychometric validation study of the Romanian translation of the Body Appreciation Scale-2 (BAS-2) conducted with Romanian university students. Study 1 involved 453 university students who completed the BAS-2 along with measures of disordered eating, self-esteem, life satisfaction, and happiness. Study 2 involved a separate sample of 109 university students who completed only the BAS-2 at two time-points three weeks apart to assess test-retest reliability. The analyses revealed a one-dimensional factor structure for BAS-2 in both women and men, with adequate fit but lack of sex invariance, and demonstrated internal consistency, convergent validity, and test-retest reliability.

2._section_summary: This Introduction section reviews the development and validation of body appreciation measures, specifically the Body Appreciation Scale (BAS) and its revised version, the Body Appreciation Scale-2 (BAS-2). The text discusses how the BAS was initially developed as a 13-item unidimensional measure but showed variable factor structures across different cultural groups, leading to the development of the 10-item BAS-2. The section documents the psychometric validation of both instruments across numerous countries and populations, including college and community samples from the U.S., Europe, Asia, and other regions, establishing that BAS-2 scores demonstrate one-dimensional factor structure with good psychometric properties across cultural groups.

8._section_summary: This section describes the statistical analyses for a single study examining the psychometric properties of the Romanian BAS-2 (Body Appreciation Scale-2). The main dataset was split into two subsamples: the first subsample (100 women and 100 men) was used for exploratory factor analysis (EFA) to assess the factor structure of BAS-2 scores separately by gender, and the second subsample (n = 243, with 112 women and 141 men) was used for confirmatory factor analysis (CFA). 17._section_summary: This discussion section presents findings from a single study examining the factor structure and validity of a Romanian translation of the BAS-2 (Body Appreciation Scale-2). The study found a one-dimensional factor structure for the BAS-2 in both women and men, though with some gender differences in factor loadings. Notably, the BAS-2 did not demonstrate full sex invariance across genders, which the authors identify as a novel finding compared to previous research. The study also reports that BAS-2 scores were significantly and negatively correlated with BMI and disordered eating symptoms, and positively correlated with self-esteem, life satisfaction, and happiness. The sample consisted of Romanian university students, limiting generalizability to the broader population.
